answer_core:
I would not grant Marcus 15% equity, CTO title, and governance rights on Friday. The risk is not only price; the package would change the company's incentive and dependency system before you know whether Marcus makes the company stronger beyond himself.

But do not make Friday a vague no. Make it a serious staged path: major upside and authority may be possible after evidence. The evidence window should test platform delivery, revenue relevance, client continuity, team dependence, knowledge transfer, and governance behavior.

Keep the middle path alive without turning the meeting into an instrument catalog. The distinction is commitment after proof versus irreversible commitment before proof.

Use exit math only as a warning about false precision. Until buyer assumptions, departure scenarios, and platform value are tested, numbers should not carry the ownership decision.

Friday message: I want to explore a serious path with you, but I cannot grant irreversible ownership and governance rights before we prove what this partnership does to the company.
